[Reasoning model — content was empty, showing reasoning]:
The user is asking about mechanical properties of blood clots (thrombi) - specifically elastic modulus, Poisson ratio, and damage parameters. They want specific published values with paper references, and they want it concise (under 400 words).

Let me recall what I know about thrombus mechanics from the literature:

**Elastic Modulus of Blood Clots:**

1. **Rana et al. (2013)** - "A physicochemical-mechanical model for the propagation of arterial thrombi" or similar work on clot mechanics. Actually, Rana et al. published work on thrombus modeling.

2. **Chueh et al. (2011)** - "Mechanical characterization of thrombi retrieved with stent retriever devices" - American Journal of Neuroradiology. They tested human clots from stroke patients. They found stiffness values around 0.5-2 kPa range... Actually I recall their values being in the kPa range.

3. **Gasser et al. (2008)** - "Failure properties of intraluminal thrombus in abdominal aortic aneurysm under static and pulsating loading" - Journal of Biomechanics. They characterized ILT (intraluminal thrombus). They used a constitutive model with fiber-reinforced behavior. Their failure stress was around 20-100 kPa depending on direction and location.

4. **Di Martino & Vorp** - earlier work on ILT mechanical properties. Di Martino et al. (1998) "Effect of intraluminal thrombus on wall stress in patient-specific models of abdominal aortic aneurysm". The ILT modulus was around 0.1-0.5 MPa? Actually ILT is quite soft, around tens to hundreds of kPa.

5. **Vorp et al. (1996)** - "Development of a non-linear finite element model of the abdominal aortic aneurysm" - ILT properties.

6. **Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2016/2017)** - work on thrombus mechanics, damage modeling. Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017) "Blood clot fracture: mechanical characterization and the constitutive modelling" - Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Biomedical Materials. They did fracture testing of blood clots and modeled with continuum damage mechanics. This is highly relevant for damage parameters!

Let me recall Fereidoonnezhad et al. 2017 more specifically: They tested porcine blood clots, performed uniaxial tension tests, and developed a hyperelastic-damage model. They used an Ogden-type strain energy function with damage variables. The damage evolution parameters... I believe they had something like α and β parameters in an exponential damage law. 

Actually, in Fereidoonnezhad et al. (2017), the damage variable d = 1 - exp(-α(β_max - β)) type formulation where β is related to maximum stretch. Hmm, I need to be careful about exact parameter values.

7. **Sugerman et al. (2021)** - "Soft matter in hard conflicts: A review of computational modelling of soft biological tissues..." no wait. Sugerman et al. have done work on thrombus modeling including damage. Sugerman et al. (2021) "Thrombus material response in ischemic stroke: a numerical study" or similar. Also Sugerman et al. (2020) "Modeling the mechanical behavior of whole blood clots using microstructural information".

8. **Malcolm et al. (2018)** - "High strain rate testing of bovine thrombus" - actually Malcolm et al. (2018) "High strain rate behavior of clots" in Annals of Biomedical Engineering? They tested at high strain rates relevant to endovascular procedures.

9
